note: Embed the query, cosine nearest-neighbours over pgvector. Strong on paraphrase and cross-lingual; blind to exact tokens like the cultivar code WL-323. The number every later stage has to beat.

Exact-term match via tsvector + ts_rank_cd. Scored 0.00 until the AND->OR tsquery fix (websearch_to_tsquery ANDs every term, so a whole-question query matched nothing). Honest result: its answer@5 edge over hybrid (0.50 vs 0.45) is a single question -- within noise at n=20 -- but doc@5 shows a real four-document gap (0.85 vs 0.65): equal-weight RRF was diluting the stronger lexical retriever's recall into the pool. That gap, not the noisy answer@5, is why the project did not stop at hybrid.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion (1/(k+60)): fuses the two rankings by position, sidestepping the incomparable cosine-vs-ts_rank score scales. Fixed q05 and q14 over the dense baseline. Gets meaning AND exact codes -- but answer@1 DROPS to 0.15 (below dense's 0.30) and mrr@5 to 0.25: equal-weight RRF pushes the true answer out of the #1 slot, buying pool recall at the cost of top-1 precision. That is exactly what the reranker exists to fix.

Re-scores the top-20 (query, chunk) candidates read together, keeps the top 5. Fixed 6 questions hybrid missed (q01, q02, q03, q09, q16, q21) with ZERO regressions -- the decisive precision win. The ordering gain answer@5 hides: answer@1 jumps 0.15->0.75 and mrr@5 0.25->0.75 -- whenever the answer is in the pool the reranker pins it to rank 1 (here answer@1 == answer@5). Still misses q07, q08, q15, q20, q22. A candidate-pool sweep (eval/sweep_candidates.py) pinpoints why: q07/q15/q20/q22 are not in hybrid's top-60 at all -- true recall gaps for the embedder lever, not pool size -- while only q08 sits deeper (hybrid rank 46), recoverable solely by tripling the candidate pool (+1 question at ~3x rerank latency, so candidates stays at 20). Measured by eval/compare_retrievers.py over the answerable golden set.

config: final cascade on the DEPLOYABLE corpus only (open+synthetic; copyrighted 'local' tier excluded)
note: The honest public-demo number a stranger actually gets. A public deployment cannot serve the copyrighted 'local' tier (3084 chunks / 11 docs, ~30% of the index), so two golden questions whose answers live only there (q06, q12) become corpus-unanswerable. Same reranker cascade, same +6 fixed / 0 regressions -- the drop from 0.75 to 0.65 is purely the smaller legal corpus, not a retrieval regression. Measured via eval/compare_retrievers.py --open-only; answer@1/mrr@5 are reported on the full index above.

config: embedder upgrade: e5-large-1024 full re-index (NOT shipped)
note: The measured embedder upgrade, run as a controlled experiment (see docs/masterclass.md 4.13). e5-large (1024-dim, 512-tok) full re-index into a parallel index. The FINAL number barely moves (0.75->0.80 = one question, within n=20 noise) -- but dense retrieval ALONE doubles: dense answer@5 0.35->0.75, dense mrr 0.33->0.72. e5's dense equals MiniLM's whole reranked cascade, so the cross-encoder had been MASKING MiniLM's weak dense; a stronger retriever relocates quality out of the expensive reranker rather than raising the final ceiling. Hypothesis FALSIFIED: predicted e5 would recover the cross-lingual misses q08/q20/q22 -- it did not (they survived MiniLM-512, MiniLM-128, AND e5); it recovered same-language q15 instead, so the residual gap is cross-lingual alignment (a query-translation lever), not embedder quality. Kept MiniLM shipped: e5 costs ~8x query-embed latency + a VECTOR(1024) migration for a noise-level final gain. The finding was the value, not the swap.

config: truncation probe: MiniLM re-chunked to 128-tok (NOT shipped)
note: The cheap probe that isolated the truncation variable: same MiniLM embedder, chunk_tokens 512->128 so no chunk exceeds the ~128-token window. Removing truncation RAISED document recall (dense doc@5 0.65->0.90 -- the model can finally see the answer text) but LOWERED the final answer@5 (0.75->0.60) and answer@1 (0.75->0.45): 4.4x more, smaller chunks dilute the exact answer chunk and starve the reranker of context. Chunk size is a precision/recall tradeoff and 512 was already near-optimal for this cascade. The obvious 'fix' made the product worse -- caught only by measuring, which is the point.

config: + query translation (bilingual retrieve + rerank; the SERVED config)
note: The query-side lever the embedder experiment pointed to, now measured (eval/query_translation.py). Translate the question to the other language (Ollama), retrieve hybrid(original) UNION hybrid(translation), rerank by the MAX cross-encoder score over both. Recovers q08 (rank None->1) -- a cross-lingual miss that survived MiniLM-512, MiniLM-128, AND e5-large -- with ZERO regressions, on the SHIPPED index. Reaches the same 0.80 as the e5 upgrade at a fraction of the cost: no re-index, no VECTOR(1024) migration, no ~8x query latency; just a translation call the app's LLM already affords (and complementary -- e5 recovered same-language q15, translation recovered cross-lingual q08). q20/q22 do NOT recover: the local 3B translator garbled domain terms (siembra->'tillage', turba->'turf'), so the residual is translation quality, not architecture. Shipped behind settings.translate_queries with soft fallback to original-only retrieval, so it can never do worse than the 0.75 baseline.
